# std.cli

<!-- Generated by `badger doc std` from the checked interfaces (badger 0.1.0). Do not edit by hand. -->

Typed command-line arguments: a record type is the interface.

    type Options = { port: Int, verbose: Bool, name: Option<String>, tag: List<String>, args: List<String> }
    let opts = cli.parse<Options>(env.args())?

Each field is an option, spelled in kebab case (`dry_run` is
`--dry-run`): `--port 8080` or `--port=8080`. A `Bool` field is a flag
(`--verbose`, `--no-verbose`; absent is false); an `Option` field may
be left out; a `List` field may repeat (`--tag a --tag b`; absent is
empty); an enum field takes one of its variant names. A field named
`args` (`List<String>`) collects the positional arguments, and `--`
ends the options. `-h`/`--help` returns a `:cli/help` error whose
`usage` is the help text; other problems are `:cli/unknown`,
`:cli/missing`, and `:cli/invalid` errors that carry it too.
